tools.name: about
tools.description: What Fron Research and its Check sites measure (saunas, bowling, trampoline parks, golf simulators, pickleball), their URLs, plans, free sample days and every document id.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Ask a question in plain language. tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Read one document by id (from search or about). sample/<site> returns that site's free example day as rows, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: data
tools.description: Structured rows from the Fron Research Data API (https://api.fronresearch.com/v1): markets, venues, bookable slots and rollups of sell-through and modeled revenue. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "data" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "agent" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: about, search · Private data: about, fetch · Public sink: data.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: about, search · Private data: about, fetch · Public sink: data

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
